candidates.name: Tsujiri

candidates.name: Kyoto Tower

candidates.reason: Valid in November, but doesn't cover the Kintetsu Nara Line used for the day trip, and pay-as-you-go ICOCA plus single Haruka tickets comes out roughly even or cheaper for this itinerary's actual mix of ~4 medium-length rides over 5 days.

candidates.name: Eikando (Zenrin-ji) Night Illumination

For anyone visiting during the temple's actual Nov 21-30 illumination window: peak crowding runs sunset to ~19:30, and entering after 20:00 gives calmer viewing (reception cutoff 21:00); the main stage and Okuno-in draw the densest crowds.

Second independent account corroborating the same window: peak crowding runs sunset to ~19:30, with 20:00+ entry called 'ideal' for avoiding crowds; a quoted firsthand account describes movement-impossible crush conditions at the two main photo spots during past peak hours.

Firsthand food-blogger account: the flashier/larger the Dotonbori signage, the more it's aimed at tourists at a markup; names Kani Doraku-style famous chains as drawing ~2-hour waits locals avoid, and recommends Aizuya (takoyaki), Daruma (kushikatsu) and Botejyu (okonomiyaki) as tested authentic alternatives instead.

Second independent firsthand account: the author explicitly avoided the famous Dotonbori-strip takoyaki shops because of inevitable lines, choosing Kouga-ryu (Amerikamura), Tako-hachi (Umeda underground) and Creole instead so she could eat without waiting the way locals do.

Kouga-ryu's Amerikamura main store (2-18-4 Nishishinsaibashi, Chuo-ku) is open 10:30-20:30 daily, extended to 10:30-21:30 on Saturdays and the day before public holidays -- confirmed on the shop's own official site.
Nanzenji's November visiting hours are 8:40-17:00 with reception closing 20 minutes before close (16:40). Main hall/garden admission ¥600. Confirmed on the temple's own site.
Nanzenji's Suirokaku aqueduct is noticeably quieter than midday during early-morning visits and in light rain, avoiding the heaviest tour-bus and day-tripper crowds.

disagreements.topic: Whether the intake's assumed anchor event (Kiyomizu-dera autumn night illumination) actually falls within the trip's Nov 13-17, 2026 dates
disagreements.investigation: Checked the temple's own official event page (kiyomizudera.or.jp/event/yakan.php) directly, corroborated by the neighborhood shopping association's page (monzenkai.com/yakan) — both independently state Nov 21-30, 2026 for the 2026 autumn night viewing, entirely after the trip's end date.
disagreements.resolution: The anchor event cannot be the trip's anchor as assumed. Kiyomizu-dera is retained as a daytime-only sight; a question card was added to the ledger for the traveler, and the days/sights content was written accordingly rather than assuming the illumination happens.

disagreements.topic: Whether physical ICOCA card sales were suspended during the 2023-24 IC-card chip shortage (an assumption stated in the research brief)
disagreements.investigation: Checked JR West's own ICOCA page (jr-odekake.net/icoca/) directly — no suspension notice found. Secondary Japanese-language coverage indicates the chip-shortage suspension affected Suica/PASMO named-card sales specifically (JR East), not ICOCA (JR West).
disagreements.resolution: The premise was likely a conflation of ICOCA with Suica/PASMO. The guide still recommends buying an ICOCA on arrival but carries an explicit ⚠ to confirm at the KIX counter, since no single source fully closed the question this pass.

disagreements.topic: Kiyomizu-dera's regular admission fee (¥500/¥200) could not be confirmed on the temple's own fetched fee page — only on its neighborhood association's page and a third-party aggregator
disagreements.investigation: Fetched kiyomizudera.or.jp/en/visit/, /en/location/, and /en/faq/ directly — none displayed the fee figure in the retrieved content (each referenced a separate page/table not resolved in this pass's fetches). monzenkai.com (the temple's neighborhood shopping association) and an aggregator (kyototravel.info) both independently state ¥500/¥200.
disagreements.resolution: Shipped as an operator-corroborated figure (tier: corroborated) rather than a directly-confirmed official one, flagged in the sight's own note for reconfirmation.

disagreements.topic: Whether Toji's autumn illumination (Pass B, T0-verified, fully covers Nov 13-17) should be woven into Day 3 (Sun Nov 15) as a substitute for the anchor event the intake assumed but that isn't running
disagreements.investigation: Pass B independently checked every plausible illumination candidate against its own official 2026 page: Kiyomizu-dera (Nov 21-30, after the trip), Eikando (night lighting from Nov 20, after the trip), and Toji (Oct 31-Dec 13, fully covers the stay). Day 3 is already the trip's most packed day -- dawn Fushimi Inari, Higashiyama, Gion, then a reserved Houshoan dinner with an unconfirmed booking window -- so adding a fourth evening stop risks the exact over-packed-day failure mode the done gate's pacing check looks for.
disagreements.resolution: Shipped Toji as its own sights entry (T0-sourced, fully verified) and flagged it in Day 3's body as an available but NOT scheduled option, with an explicit note pointing to the ledger's traveler question rather than silently cramming it into an already-packed day or silently dropping a genuinely strong find.

saturation.note: Merged view of both passes at reconcile. Pass A: late-round Osaka food searches (Chukasoba Kazura, Fukutaro, additional battera/sushi spots) mostly surfaced options redundant with already-shortlisted picks or too weakly sourced to ship. Kyoto/Nara sights searches converged on the same marquee stops with consistent crowd-timing advice. Pass B: native-language searches surfaced one genuinely new, strong, T0-verifiable finding (Toji as an anchor-quality substitute) and several corroborating/alternative food and quiet-spot leads (Kouga-ryu, Nanzenji, Asajigahara-en); by its final round, further native-language searches were returning the same aggregator listicles and already-captured venue names. Remaining unresolved items across both passes (the JR Nara Line's exact official fare page, Nara National Museum's blocked official page, a few restaurant hours, Houshoan's exact booking window) are backbone-confirmation gaps, not open questions that would change which candidates ship — flagged as ⚠ in the guide rather than blocking this pass. The one open question that COULD change the itinerary shape (whether to build Toji into Day 3) is recorded as a traveler question rather than resolved unilaterally. A later reconcile attempt re-checked every objective claim against the evidence-kind/source-kind law: climbed to a genuine official source for Abaraya (its own gorp.jp site) and confirmed Wanaka's official/operator sites are both certificate-blocked (not just unfetched); reclassified ekitan.com as a canonical fare reference rather than a review aggregator; found and used the official Nara Deer Preservation Foundation page for the rutting-season risk note; found two fresh independent firsthand sources for Fushimi Inari's crowd timing and a fresh second firsthand source for Asajigahara-en (replacing an 11-year-old first source that turned out to be stale); and removed a handful of claims (the Gion private-road ban's fine amount/date, the Bamboo Grove's specific crowd-timing window, Gion Nishikawa's price) that could not be climbed to a compliant source within this pass's budget — those stay as honest gaps (omitted from evidence.v2.json; the Gion ban remains in the guide's own sight body on its press citation, which this evidence-kind law does not gate).

nativeLanguage.why: English coverage of Kyoto/Osaka/Nara is dominated by generic top-10 tourist content and tour-operator marketing pages (confirmed directly for Fushimi Inari). Native-Japanese searches were needed to reach resident blogs on crowd timing and tourist-trap food, to catch a stale-year illumination-date trap that English aggregator content was also repeating, and to surface a manners/legal reality (the Gion photo-ban) that doesn't show up in English tourist material at all.
